fixes.explanation: Music it is, friend. David, Israel's king, put these Levites in charge of the music in the house of the LORD after the ark rested there (1 Chronicles 6:31). A bakery needs a little song too, because nobody gets through a long batch in silence. Mine is mostly humming and a timer that doesn't care.

Gates are a real job, but they aren't the one in this verse. The text says David put these men in charge of the music in the house of the LORD after the ark rested there (1 Chronicles 6:31). Music is the job the verse gives them. Save the gate duty for somebody else.

Tabernacle, yes! The singers ministered with song before the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, until Solomon built the house of the LORD in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 6:32). The verse tells us exactly where they sang and how long. I like a clear schedule, and I know a thing or two about being put in a spot and told to get to work.

I see why you'd pick the palace, since David was king. But the text says they ministered with song before the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting (1 Chronicles 6:32). The palace never comes up in this verse. The tabernacle is the place it names.

A gate would make a fine stage, friend, but that's not what the verse says. The singers ministered with song before the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, until Solomon built the house of the LORD in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 6:32). The tabernacle is the place the text names. A gate isn't mentioned at all.

Good thinking, since David was the one who put them in charge (1 Chronicles 6:31). But the verse never says they waited on the king. It says they performed their duties "…according to the regulations given them." (1 Chronicles 6:32) That's the standard the text gives, and the king's presence isn't part of it.

Yes, friend! The text says they come first "…because the first lot fell to them…" (1 Chronicles 6:54) So it came down to the lot. Nobody had to argue over who goes first, and I wish deciding who gets the first cookie off the tray were that easy.

Biggest first sounds reasonable, but this verse doesn't say a word about size. It says "…because the first lot fell to them…" (1 Chronicles 6:54) The lot is the reason the text gives. Clan size never comes up.
